newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says troops authorized to go to Kuwait.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says troops authorized to go to Kuwait.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Tuesday he has signed orders to deploy U.S. troops to Kuwait but did not say when they might actually go.

"I authorized the deploymeht last weekend and ... the deployment orders were signed last night," Clinton told reporters in denying reports that he might have decided against deploying 3,000 to 5,000 U.S. Army troops to Kuwait as a show of strength in the U.S. military showdwon with Iraq.

The Washington Post reported on Tuesday that Clinton was reconsidering his decision on the deployment since the showdown with Iraqi President Saddam Hussein seemed to be easing. But Clinton said he meant to pursue that aspect of his vow to reenforce U.S. military muscle in the Gulf region.

"I was surprised when I read the story today (about possible cancellation of the troop deployment) and I asked for an explanation of it and none of our people had one because I asked for the deployment last weekend and, as I said, the orders were signed last night," he said.

The president also defended his course of action in ordering two cruise missile strikes against southern Iraqi anti-aircraft defences two weeks ago in retaliation for an Iraqi move against Kurds in the north. That strategy has drawn criticism from U.S. Republicans, some of whom indicated they remained sceptical after the White House briefing on Tuesday.

"We did the appropriate thing in the appropriate way and we've gotten the results that we sought," Clinton told reporters. He also expressed satisfaction at the response Defence Secretary William Perry had received from leaders of Gulf states during a mission to that region last weekend designed to seek support for the U.S. intervention. He gave no details, however.
